clue.text: Name of monarchs, primarily John, Anne, Mary, Elizabeth and Stephen

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following name is used

parts.words: John, Anne, Mary, Elizabeth and Stephen
parts.note: initials of the five royal names

explanation.surface: A list of English monarchs offered as examples of a royal name.
explanation.walkthrough: Every name listed belonged to an English monarch, and so does the answer: two kings of England and seven of Scotland bore it.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of England and Scotland bore this first name, so it is a regal name.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: merely, as an adverb
second meaning: equitable, as an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, as if something were merely fair, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means merely as an adverb and morally right or equitable as an adjective.

wordplay.note: MI and RE, two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Jotted observations about a stretch of marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mire is a swamp or patch of deep mud and wet ground.

clue.text: Food Molly Malone sells she will char?

parts.note: contracted as she'll
the char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Molly Malone will cook what she sells.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the Dublin street seller in the song, crying 'cockles and mussels'. 'char' looks like a verb, to scorch, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles and mussels, her wares in the song, are both kinds of seafood with shells.

clue.text: Delighted to do work cleaning Mediterranean

parts.note: to char is to work as a cleaner, a British usage
common short form of the sea's name

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to take a cleaning job by the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: A char or charwoman is a British word for a cleaner, and to char is to do that work.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed is an adjective meaning greatly pleased, a close synonym of delighted.

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the extraterrestrial from the film

explanation.surface: An odd sect that eats extraterrestrial food.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a cut of meat or a shaped patty, an example of food.

clue.text: Source of light in the middle of equinox month

indicators.note: the middle of a word is what is left without its ends, so only the central letters count

parts.note: the spring equinox falls in March; its central letters

explanation.surface: Where light comes from at the midpoint of an equinoctial month.
explanation.walkthrough: The northern spring equinox is in March, so that is the month meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces bright light from an electric spark between electrodes.

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the capital of Spain
gal is informal for girl; the 's is the link 'has'

explanation.surface: A song belonging to a girl from a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices, popular in the Renaissance.

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a date is a romantic meeting
the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's romantic meeting outside the school gates goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' suggests going sour or leaving, but here it means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: When a bomb goes off it explodes, which is what detonate means intransitively.

clue.text: Dragon exhausted eating queen quite recently

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside itself, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: spent means used up or tired out
Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of the queen who reigned until 2022

explanation.surface: A dragon that has only just tired itself out by devouring a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite recently' qualifies the queen: ER was the reigning monarch's cipher until 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth and older English a dragon is a great snake-like beast, and serpent was used for such monsters.

indicators.note: doing something strangely means doing it in an odd, disordered way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee behaved oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person in training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Isolated state of country after a deception

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first in the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
a lie is a deception
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A nation left isolated after being lied to.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the condition of being estranged or cut off from others.

clue.text: A hepcat? It is awful cool

indicators.note: awful means very bad, so the letters before it are in a bad state and must be rebuilt

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a jazz fan is terribly cool.
explanation.walkthrough: A hepcat is old slang for a hip jazz fan, so 'cool' reads as stylish; here it means lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cool towards something is to show little interest, which is being indifferent.

clue.text: Demanding deep study on behalf of institute

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
to found is to establish

explanation.surface: A project needing serious research is carried out for an institute.
explanation.definitionFit: A profound idea is deep and needs much thought to grasp.

parts.note: I'm, as someone owning up
mature means grown up or of advanced years

explanation.surface: A naive person confesses to being older.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession 'I'm mature' is written as one word that means the very opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature means childish and lacking experience, which is close to naive.

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to rein in is to control
familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A child told to stay with mother, who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay where one is, a direct synonym of the verb.

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A seasonal worker with nothing to do during the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant house or post is empty, with nobody occupying it.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who naps, from kip, British slang for sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for sleep, so a sleeper can be one who kips; 'cured' suggests healing but means smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a salted smoked herring and, playfully, a person taking a kip.

clue.text: What can relieve the gloom of strike during journey by air

indicators.note: during places one thing within the span of another, so one word goes inside

parts.note: a flight is a journey by plane
to lash is to strike

explanation.surface: Something to cheer passengers whose air journey is hit by a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloom' reads as low spirits, but it means darkness here.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch dispels darkness, which is the literal gloom it relieves.

indicators.note: not quite finished means the end is missing, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a thing is an item; 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A delicate piece that has been left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine thread or sand is thin or slender, the sense of narrowness.

indicators.note: not tells us a letter for the following word is left out

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Troops behaving very stupidly, though not the British ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers, collectively.

clue.text: Typical guest unable to be regularly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring letters at regular intervals means every other one is skipped

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A guest who can't come is routinely overlooked, as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means normal or customary, which is what typical describes.

parts.note: standard abbreviation of the city
British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles freeway severely affected by something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is informal for thrash or beat soundly.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter
second meaning: a large jug for pouring

explanation.surface: A baseball player locked up in jail, jug being slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in jug' suggests prison slang, but jug is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the baseball thrower and a large container with a lip for pouring liquids.

clue.text: Suspect male reader is one into fantasy

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not right, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: standard abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who reads is suspected of preferring fantasy fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone given to fanciful imaginings rather than reality.

clue.text: Child's first with yen for American sweets

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter
and means with or plus
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A child keen above all to get American sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a craving, fitting the child, but it is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for what Britons call sweets.
